tasks.title: Scaffold the .NET API and the Angular app
tasks.description: The repository is empty apart from .team/ and .gitignore. Create the two projects described under Layout in the guidelines, wired together and testable, with no notes features yet. Backend: an ASP.NET Core Web API (controllers) in backend/Notes.Api and an xUnit project in backend/Notes.Api.Tests, both in backend/Notes.sln; one endpoint GET /api/health returning {"status":"ok"}; CORS or a dev proxy so the Angular dev server can call the API. Frontend: a new Angular app in frontend/ (standalone components, strict mode, routing, plain CSS, no SSR) whose home page calls /api/health through a service and shows whether the API is reachable. Add a root README.md with the commands to run and test both sides.
acceptance: dotnet build backend succeeds with no warnings
dotnet test backend passes and includes a WebApplicationFactory test proving GET /api/health returns 200 with {"status":"ok"}
frontend/package.json has a test:ci script that runs all tests once, headless, and (cd frontend && npm run test:ci) passes
(cd frontend && npm run build) succeeds
The home page shows 'API: online' when the health call succeeds and 'API: offline' when it fails, and both cases are covered by a component or service test
git status is clean after building and testing both projects (build output is ignored, not committed)
README.md documents how to run the API, run the frontend, and run all tests

tasks.title: Notes API: create, list, get, update, delete
tasks.description: Add a Note resource to the backend. A note has id (integer, generated), title (required, 1-100 characters after trimming), body (optional, up to 2000 characters), createdAt and updatedAt (UTC, set by the server). Store notes with EF Core in a SQLite file; create the database automatically on startup. Endpoints: GET /api/notes (newest first), GET /api/notes/{id}, POST /api/notes, PUT /api/notes/{id}, DELETE /api/notes/{id}. Follow the backend rules in the guidelines: thin controllers, a NotesService, DTO records. Backend only; do not touch frontend/.
acceptance: POST /api/notes with a valid title returns 201, a Location header, and the created note including id, createdAt and updatedAt
POST or PUT with a missing, empty, whitespace-only or over-100-character title returns 400 with a problem-details body; a body over 2000 characters also returns 400
GET /api/notes returns all notes ordered by createdAt, newest first; an empty database returns 200 with []
GET, PUT and DELETE on an id that does not exist return 404
PUT changes title and body, updates updatedAt, and leaves createdAt unchanged
DELETE returns 204 and the note is gone from later GET requests
Every rule above is covered by a WebApplicationFactory test using in-memory SQLite, and dotnet test backend passes
The SQLite database file is git-ignored and is not committed

tasks.title: Notes page: list, add and delete notes
tasks.description: Build the notes UI in the Angular app on top of the API from T2. Add a NotesService for all /api/notes calls and a notes page at the route /notes (make / redirect to it; keep the API status indicator visible in the page header). The page lists notes newest first, showing title, body and created date, has a form to add a note (title and body), and a delete button on each note that asks for confirmation. Frontend only; do not change the API contract.
acceptance: Opening /notes loads and shows the notes from GET /api/notes, newest first
With no notes, the page shows the text 'No notes yet'
Submitting the form with a valid title creates the note through the API, the new note appears at the top without a page reload, and the form is cleared
The add button is disabled, or a validation message is shown, when the title is empty, only spaces, or longer than 100 characters; no request is sent in that case
Deleting a note asks for confirmation, calls DELETE, and removes it from the list; cancelling the confirmation does nothing
If loading, creating or deleting fails, a visible error message is shown and the list is left unchanged
Components do not use HttpClient directly; NotesService and the notes page have tests for the cases above, and npm run test:ci passes

tasks.title: Edit notes and search by text
tasks.description: Two additions that touch both sides. Search: GET /api/notes accepts an optional q query parameter and returns only notes whose title or body contains q, case-insensitive; the notes page gets a search box that filters the list through the API as the user types (debounced, about 300 ms). Edit: each note on the page gets an Edit button that turns it into an inline form for title and body with Save and Cancel, using PUT /api/notes/{id} and the same validation rules as creating a note.
acceptance: GET /api/notes?q=milk returns only notes with 'milk' in the title or body, in any letter case; q that is empty or only spaces behaves like no q
Backend tests cover a match in the title, a match in the body, case-insensitivity, and no matches (200 with [])
Typing in the search box updates the list from the API after a short pause, sends one request per pause rather than one per keystroke, and clearing the box shows all notes again
When a search has no results the page shows 'No notes match your search', which is different from the 'No notes yet' text
Edit, change the title, Save: the note shows the new title without a page reload and stays in the same position in the list
Cancel restores the original text and sends no request; Save with an invalid title shows a validation message and sends no request
If saving fails, a visible error is shown and the note stays in edit mode with the user's text
dotnet test backend and npm run test:ci both pass with tests for the behaviour above
